cand.title: 72nd Annual Conference & Marketplace — Intersections
cand.excerpt: Annual professional conference and marketplace in downtown Toronto with workshops, tours, exhibitors, receptions and multi-day programming. This is a direct fit for meeting rooms, breakfast/refreshment packages, breakouts and private dining; local day delegates can generate venue revenue even though the event also promotes accommodation.
cand.selectionWhy: Prior blocked-promising candidate (no exact date/contact in thin ledger)

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Lul Teklit, Senior Meeting Manager, is the strongest sourcing-path contact: her official biography covers planning and implementing IDA events, and the 2026 conference explicitly names her for accommodation-legitimacy questions. Allison Shashok, Vice President of Membership, Marketing & Operations, is a second relevant organizer relationship/operations contact; the event names her for media credentials, not hotel procurement. Neither source establishes final hotel-contract signing authority.
findings.futureEdition: IDA officially lists the 73rd Annual Conference & Marketplace for 6–8 October 2027 in Houston, Texas, United States. Exact venue and lodging arrangements were not verified in accessible official material; venue remains null. This is not a Toronto edition. No officially published 2028 edition or future Toronto return was located. The Toronto dates, 1–3 September 2026, are activity dates, not publication dates, and fall before the 6 December 2026–June 2028 opportunity horizon.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using supplied hotel specifications: the 157-room Radisson is not a sole-host solution for a conference promoted to over 1,300 people; its approximately 240-theatre largest room cannot hold the full conference. A downtown waterfront city hotel is more suitable than a destination resort for this urban place-management programme. Historically plausible roles were delegate/speaker overflow, VIP lodging and appropriately sized ancillary meetings, not displacement of the Westin main programme. The edition-specific Radisson discount is stronger fit evidence than proximity alone, but no actual Radisson room pickup, catered function or meeting booking was published. The supplied 15–109-peak-room target is a sales-sizing constraint, not measured event demand. Do not offer breakfast, private dining or reception catering until the hotel confirms current restaurant/lounge and banquet-service capability.
findings.venueCommitments: 2026: The Westin Harbour Castle, Toronto, 1 Harbour Square, Toronto, Ontario M5J 1A6, plus various downtown Toronto locations. This is Toronto proper, in the downtown waterfront territory, and a competing hotel, not MTCC or Exhibition Place as the main venue. The agenda assigns conference sessions and marketplace space to the Westin. Historical venue confirmation is not open meeting inventory. 2027 Houston venue: unverified.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified edition sequence: 70th, Seattle, 11–13 September 2024, Hyatt Regency Seattle; 71st, Washington, DC, 24–27 September 2025, Capital Hilton; 72nd, Toronto, 1–3 September 2026, The Westin Harbour Castle; 73rd announced for Houston, 6–8 October 2027, venue unverified. This demonstrates an annual, rotating-city series, not an annual Toronto booking or a verified Toronto return interval.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2026 was an organizer-published host/overflow hotel pathway, not an identified housing bureau or open RFP. Official wording: “The official conference accommodation is at The Westin Harbour Castle, Toronto”; “The overflow hotel is at the Delta Hotels Toronto”; and “The room block has been completed at both hotels.” The page says attendees could call about cancellations, which does not establish sellout or additional open inventory. Every other hotel named in its suggested-accommodation sections: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown; Le Germain Hotel Toronto Maple Leaf Square; Fairmont Royal York; Omni King Edward; InterContinental Toronto Centre. These are not stated to be contracted blocks. Importantly, the same edition page specifically advertises Radisson: “Use IDA Code ‘BTGZUN’ for 10% off the prevailing hotel rate by August 13, 2026,” prepaid and nonrefundable. This proves an edition-specific promotional pathway, not room allotment, pickup or a block guarantee. The page also says “IDA is not working with any third parties to offer attendees accommodation.” 2027 housing is unverified.
findings.organizationStructure: IDA is the membership association and event owner/organizer, not a hotel, corporate meeting owner, PCO or DMC. The 2026 edition names the Downtown Toronto BIA Alliance and City of Toronto as co-hosts. The Westin is the host venue/hotel; Delta is the named overflow hotel. No external PCO or housing bureau was identified; the explicit third-party-housing disclaimer concerns accommodation, not proof that no outside event supplier exists.
findings.competitiveLimitations: 2026 main venue and official lodging were already directed to the Westin, with Delta explicitly designated overflow. Radisson was a suggested alternative with a discount code, not the official overflow hotel. Explicit overflow provision is sourced, but neither overflow volume, sellout, unmet demand, displacement nor Radisson production is established. The past edition cannot generate new 2026 sales; the next announced edition is in Houston.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Lul Teklit first, referencing the 2026 BTGZUN promotion, to request a post-event review of Radisson usage and the route for future Toronto accommodation or ancillary-meeting sourcing. Include Allison Shashok for relationship continuity, not as an assumed procurement authority. Internally reconcile the promotion with reservations/revenue records and any IDA correspondence before claiming a prior booking relationship. Ask about an actual Toronto return or separately scheduled local programme and its decision timetable; do not send an unsolicited 2027 Toronto block proposal. Keep out of the active event-demand pipeline unless new qualifying Toronto dates and requirements are supplied.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: As of 15 November 2026, the Toronto edition is past. Do not qualify it as live local catering/day-meeting or accommodation demand. The confirmed 2027 Houston edition is within the time horizon but outside this Toronto hotel’s territory. Its lodging-sourcing status is unconfirmed, not open.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: retain as a historical relationship-development account because IDA already published an edition-specific Radisson offer. A future Toronto edition or a separately confirmed Toronto IDA meeting could support competitive overflow or ancillary-meeting capture, but neither is established. Rotating annual recurrence alone does not justify forecasting Toronto business through June 2028.
